requirements.quote:
As keys at a given encryption level become available to TLS, TLS
   indicates to QUIC that reading or writing keys at that encryption
   level are available.
requirements.condition: When reading keys at an encryption level become available to TLS
requirements.required_behavior: TLS indicates to QUIC that reading keys at that encryption level are available.
requirements.why_checkable: A TLS-to-QUIC key-availability callback or event can be observed for each encryption level and read direction.

requirements.quote:
As keys at a given encryption level become available to TLS, TLS
   indicates to QUIC that reading or writing keys at that encryption
   level are available.
requirements.condition: When writing keys at an encryption level become available to TLS
requirements.required_behavior: TLS indicates to QUIC that writing keys at that encryption level are available.
requirements.why_checkable: A TLS-to-QUIC key-availability callback or event can be observed for each encryption level and write direction.

requirements.quote:
The availability of new keys is always a result of providing inputs
   to TLS.  TLS only provides new keys after being initialized (by a
   client) or when provided with new handshake data.
requirements.condition: When TLS makes new keys available
requirements.required_behavior: Make the keys available only as a result of input to TLS, after client-side initialization or after new handshake data is provided.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Provide new keys without client-side initialization or new handshake data having supplied the triggering TLS input.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can record TLS inputs and assert that every new-key event follows one of the stated triggering inputs.

requirements.quote:
While waiting for TLS processing to
   complete, an endpoint SHOULD buffer received packets if they might be
   processed using keys that are not yet available.
requirements.condition: While waiting for TLS processing to complete, when a received packet might be processable with keys that are not yet available
requirements.required_behavior: Buffer the received packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A delayed-key test can inject such a packet and inspect whether the endpoint retains it pending TLS processing.

requirements.quote:
These packets can
   be processed once keys are provided by TLS.
requirements.condition: When TLS provides the keys needed by packets buffered while TLS processing was incomplete
requirements.required_behavior: Make the buffered packets eligible for processing after the keys are provided.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Process the buffered packets using the unavailable keys before those keys are provided.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can delay key delivery and verify that packet processing is deferred until the key-provision event and enabled afterward.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint SHOULD
   continue to respond to packets that can be processed during this
   time.
requirements.condition: While waiting for TLS processing to complete, when a received packet can be processed with currently available keys
requirements.required_behavior: Continue responding to the processable packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can hold TLS processing pending, deliver a packet decryptable with existing keys, and observe whether the endpoint responds.

requirements.quote:
TLS provides QUIC with three items as a new encryption level becomes
   available:

   *  A secret
requirements.condition: When a new encryption level becomes available
requirements.required_behavior: TLS provides QUIC with a secret for that encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: The TLS-to-QUIC interface can be observed to verify that a secret accompanies each new encryption-level event.

requirements.quote:
TLS provides QUIC with three items as a new encryption level becomes
   available:

   *  A secret

   *  An Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) function
requirements.condition: When a new encryption level becomes available
requirements.required_behavior: TLS provides QUIC with an AEAD function for that encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: The TLS-to-QUIC interface can be observed to verify that an AEAD selection accompanies each new encryption-level event.

requirements.quote:
TLS provides QUIC with three items as a new encryption level becomes
   available:

   *  A secret

   *  An Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) function

   *  A Key Derivation Function (KDF)
requirements.condition: When a new encryption level becomes available
requirements.required_behavior: TLS provides QUIC with a KDF for that encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: The TLS-to-QUIC interface can be observed to verify that a KDF selection accompanies each new encryption-level event.

requirements.quote: These values are based on the values that TLS negotiates
requirements.condition: When TLS provides the secret for a new encryption level
requirements.required_behavior: Base the supplied secret on the values negotiated by TLS.
requirements.why_checkable: A negotiated-suite test can compare the supplied secret and its derivation context with the TLS negotiation result.

requirements.quote: These values are based on the values that TLS negotiates
requirements.condition: When TLS provides the AEAD function for a new encryption level
requirements.required_behavior: Select the supplied AEAD function based on the values negotiated by TLS.
requirements.why_checkable: The AEAD identifier exposed to QUIC can be compared with the TLS cipher suite selected by negotiation.

requirements.quote: These values are based on the values that TLS negotiates
requirements.condition: When TLS provides the KDF for a new encryption level
requirements.required_behavior: Select the supplied KDF based on the values negotiated by TLS.
requirements.why_checkable: The KDF identifier exposed to QUIC can be compared with the hash/KDF selected by TLS negotiation.

requirements.quote:
These values are based on the values that TLS negotiates and are used
   by QUIC to generate packet and header protection keys
requirements.condition: When generating packet-protection keys for a TLS-established encryption level
requirements.required_behavior: QUIC uses the TLS-provided secret, AEAD function, and KDF values to generate the packet-protection keys.
requirements.why_checkable: Derived packet-protection keys can be compared with outputs computed from the TLS-provided inputs.

requirements.quote:
These values are based on the values that TLS negotiates and are used
   by QUIC to generate packet and header protection keys
requirements.condition: When generating header-protection keys for a TLS-established encryption level
requirements.required_behavior: QUIC uses the TLS-provided secret, AEAD function, and KDF values to generate the header-protection keys.
requirements.why_checkable: Derived header-protection keys can be compared with outputs computed from the TLS-provided inputs.

requirements.quote:
If 0-RTT is possible, it is ready after the client sends a TLS
   ClientHello message or the server receives that message.
requirements.condition: On a client where 0-RTT is possible, after the client sends its TLS ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: Treat 0-RTT as ready for use.
requirements.why_checkable: A client handshake trace can correlate the ClientHello send event with the transition to 0-RTT readiness.

requirements.quote:
If 0-RTT is possible, it is ready after the client sends a TLS
   ClientHello message or the server receives that message.
requirements.condition: On a server where 0-RTT is possible, after the server receives the TLS ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: Treat 0-RTT as ready for use.
requirements.why_checkable: A server handshake trace can correlate ClientHello receipt with the transition to 0-RTT readiness.

requirements.quote:
If the Finished
   message is lost, the endpoint uses the Handshake encryption level to
   retransmit the lost message.
requirements.condition: When a Finished message sent at the Handshake encryption level is lost
requirements.required_behavior: Retransmit the lost Finished message using the Handshake encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss-injection test can inspect the encryption level of the retransmitted Finished message.

requirements.quote:
Reordering or loss of packets can mean
   that QUIC will need to handle packets at multiple encryption levels.
   During the handshake, this means potentially handling packets at
   higher and lower encryption levels than the current encryption level
   used by TLS.
requirements.condition: During the handshake, when reordering or loss delivers a packet at an encryption level higher than TLS's current encryption level
requirements.required_behavior: QUIC handles the packet at the higher encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-reordering tests can deliver a higher-level packet while TLS is at a lower level and observe QUIC processing.

requirements.quote:
Reordering or loss of packets can mean
   that QUIC will need to handle packets at multiple encryption levels.
   During the handshake, this means potentially handling packets at
   higher and lower encryption levels than the current encryption level
   used by TLS.
requirements.condition: During the handshake, when reordering or loss delivers a packet at an encryption level lower than TLS's current encryption level
requirements.required_behavior: QUIC handles the packet at the lower encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-reordering tests can deliver a lower-level packet after TLS advances and observe QUIC processing.

requirements.quote:
In particular, server implementations need to be able to read packets
   at the Handshake encryption level at the same time as the 0-RTT
   encryption level.
requirements.condition: While a server is accepting 0-RTT packets during the handshake
requirements.required_behavior: Remain able to read packets at the Handshake encryption level concurrently with packets at the 0-RTT encryption level.
requirements.why_checkable: A server test can interleave valid 0-RTT and Handshake-protected packets and verify that both are readable without a key-level switch disabling either.

requirements.quote:
A client could interleave ACK frames that are
   protected with Handshake keys with 0-RTT data, and the server needs
   to process those acknowledgments in order to detect lost Handshake
   packets.
requirements.condition: When a client interleaves Handshake-key-protected ACK frames with 0-RTT data
requirements.required_behavior: The server processes those ACK frames so that it can detect lost Handshake packets.
requirements.why_checkable: An interleaving test can verify ACK processing and the resulting Handshake loss-detection state at the server.

requirements.quote:
QUIC also needs access to keys that might not ordinarily be available
   to a TLS implementation.  For instance, a client might need to
   acknowledge Handshake packets before it is ready to send CRYPTO
   frames at that encryption level.  TLS therefore needs to provide keys
   to QUIC before it might produce them for its own use.
requirements.condition: When QUIC needs an encryption-level key before TLS is ready to use that key itself
requirements.required_behavior: TLS provides the key to QUIC before producing it for TLS's own use.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Delay exposing the key to QUIC until TLS is ready to use it itself.
requirements.why_checkable: Event ordering can be instrumented to verify that the TLS-to-QUIC key delivery precedes TLS's own use-ready event.
